newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Fujimori vows no "acts of blood" in siege.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori vows no "acts of blood" in siege.

text.p: President Alberto Fujimori said on Tuesday he remained firm against "blackmail" by rebels holding hostages in Peru but would ensure the safety of the 74 hostages.
"The life of the hostages is assured -- their physical well-being -- because there are not going to be acts of blood," Fujimori told reporters during a surprise visit to a Lima shantytown.

Asked what his current position was in the crisis, he replied: "A mixture of firmness in our position -- and in this sense the non-liberation of MRTA (Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement) prisoners -- and at the same time prudence."
He added, "We maintain a firm position of not giving in to blackmail from the terrorists."
Fujimori, who previously had spoken in public only twice since MRTA rebels stormed the Japanese ambassador's residence on Dec. 17, said, "We must look for a way out of the crisis."

The president had stopped his regular visits to the capital's shantytowns when the crisis broke but he said he ventured out on Tuesday to show the world "terrorism" had not paralysed Peru and the country was continuing normally. He also visited a local jail as part of a frenetic tour of the city.
"We should not transmit the image that in Peru we are living a situation of terrorism," he said.

The rebels are demanding the government free their more than 400 jailed comrades, but Fujimori has rejected the demand and said he would look for a "way out" that did not use force only if the MRTA releases all the hostages and laid down their arms.

Progress toward a solution seemed at a standstill on Tuesday. After freeing more than 430 hostages, the rebels have not released any for six days and Education Minister Domingo Palermo, the government negotiator, has not re-entered the building since a first face-to-face meeting with the guerrillas on Dec. 28.
But Fujimori said he was hopeful of a bloodless end to the three-week siege. "Like everyone, I hope for a peaceful solution," he said.
